original_interpretation: Dutch national export authorisation for advanced SME, starting with DUV lithography, in force since 1 Sep 2023.
evidence_found: "This new authorisation requirement builds on the existing national export control rules that have been in force since 1 September 2023. They apply to a very specific technology in the semiconductor manufacturing process: deep ultraviolet lithography equipment." (Government.nl news item, 06-09-2024, para 1)
notes: Re-opened in browser. Government source (tier 1) describing its own measure. Later Dutch expansions (e.g. 2025) not checked here.

original_interpretation: Dutch minister expanded national licence requirement for advanced SME to non-EU destinations effective 7 Sep 2024.
evidence_found: "As of 7 September 2024, the national export control measure applicable to advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment will be expanded, making more types of equipment subject to a national authorisation requirement. The change was announced by Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Reinette Klever" ... "The national measure applies to exports from the Netherlands to destinations outside the EU." (Government.nl, 06-09-2024)
correction: The 7 Sep 2024 change expanded the set of equipment types covered (more SME made subject to authorisation); it did not newly extend the measure to non-EU destinations. The measure applies to exports from the Netherlands to destinations outside the EU. Announced by Minister Reinette Klever in Staatscourant 2024, 29008. See new superseding claim.
notes: Claim wording implies the destination scope was what changed; source says the equipment scope changed.

original_interpretation: Aug 2025: US government to take 9.9% Intel stake (433.3m shares at USD 20.47), funded by USD 5.7bn unpaid CHIPS grants + USD 3.2bn Secure Enclave.
evidence_found: "the government agrees to purchase 433.3 million primary shares of Intel common stock at a price of $20.47 per share, equivalent to a 9.9 percent stake"; "funded by the remaining $5.7 billion in grants previously awarded, but not yet paid, to Intel under the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act and $3.2 billion awarded ... Secure Enclave program" (Intel 8-K Ex. 99.1)
notes: Opened original on sec.gov via web_extract (browser blocked by SEC). Total USD 8.9bn matches metric. Release adds this is on top of USD 2.2bn CHIPS grants already received (USD 11.1bn total). Deal closing/terms after announcement not checked.

original_interpretation: 26 USC 48D applies to facilities whose primary purpose is making semiconductors or SME; no credit for property whose construction begins after 31 Dec 2026.
evidence_found: "the term 'advanced manufacturing facility' means a facility for which the primary purpose is the manufacturing of semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment" (48D(b)(3)); "(e) Termination of credit: The credit allowed under this section shall not apply to property the construction of which begins after December 31, 2026."
notes: uscode.house.gov prelim (laws in effect 17 Sep 2026) opened via web_extract but sections were elided and the site was 'under maintenance' in browser; full (b)(3) and (e) text read on the Cornell LII mirror of the same section (law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/48D), wording identical. No extension of the 2026 construction deadline found as of 2026-10-01 (secondary sources and TechTimes 3 Sep 2026 say no legislation passed). Re-check before 31 Dec 2026.

original_interpretation: 7 Oct 2022 BIS IFR (87 FR 62186) amended EAR to control advanced computing ICs and SME items for China.
evidence_found: Abstract: "BIS is amending the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to implement necessary controls on advanced computing integrated circuits (ICs), computer commodities that contain such ICs, and certain semiconductor manufacturing items." FR API: action "Interim final rule; request for comments.", citation "87 FR 62186", effective_on 2022-10-07, published 2022-10-13.
notes: Some instructions effective 7 Oct, others 12 and 21 Oct 2022 (DATES section).

original_interpretation: Oct 2022 rule requires US persons to obtain licence for certain activities supporting development/production of certain ICs in China.
evidence_found: "BIS is also informing the public that specific activities of \"U.S. persons\" that `support' the \"development\" or \"production\" of certain ICs in the PRC require a license." (FR 2022-21658 abstract)

original_interpretation: Oct 2022 rule created two new FDP rules (advanced computing, supercomputers) and expanded licence requirements for 28 China-based Entity List entities.
evidence_found: "(3) creating two new Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rules related to advanced computing and 'supercomputers' and expanding an existing FDP rule for certain entities listed on the Entity List"; "This rule expands the scope of licensing requirements for 28 existing entities on the Entity List that are located in the PRC and were added to the Entity List between 2015 and 2021." (FR 2022-21658, Supplementary Information)
notes: Expansion for the 28 entities is via the Entity List FDP rule (foreign-produced items).

original_interpretation: BIS IFR effective 2 Dec 2024 (89 FR 96790) added new FDP rules for SME, expanded SME controls, and created HBM controls (ECCN 3A090.c).
evidence_found: Abstract: "adding new controls for certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment ... creating new Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rules for certain commodities to impair the capability to produce 'advanced-node integrated circuits' ... adding new controls for certain high bandwidth memory"; "C. Addition of HBM controls, including addition of new ECCN 3A090.c"; "This rule is effective December 2, 2024." citation 89 FR 96790.
notes: Two new FDP rules: SME FDP and Footnote 5 (FN5) FDP. Several compliance dates were 31 Dec 2024. HBM bandwidth-density threshold not re-read (page truncated); not part of the claim text.

original_interpretation: Sep 2025 BIS affiliates rule made entities >=50% owned by Entity List parties automatically subject to Entity List restrictions.
evidence_found: "On September 30, 2025, ... BIS published the interim final rule, 'Expansion of End-User Controls to Cover Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities' (90 FR 47201) (Affiliates Rule). Under the Affiliates Rule, any entity that is at least 50 percent owned directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, by one or more entities on the Entity List, or by unlisted entities that are subject to license requirements ... is itself automatically subject to Entity List restrictions." (FR 2025-19846, Background)
notes: Rule also reached affiliates of other restricted parties (MEU list, certain OFAC programs per secondary sources). Rule has been suspended since 10 Nov 2025 (see CLM-0306); should not be presented as currently in effect.

original_interpretation: BIS suspended the affiliates rule 10 Nov 2025-9 Nov 2026; reinstated automatically 10 Nov 2026 unless further action.
evidence_found: "The first phase, effective on November 10, 2025, and ending November 9, 2026, is a one-year suspension of the Affiliates Rule ... In the second phase of this final rule, effective November 10, 2026 and extending indefinitely, the changes included in the Affiliates Rule ... will be added back into the EAR." Abstract: "The suspension is set to end November 9, 2026, absent a future extension." (FR 2025-19846, 90 FR 50857)
notes: As of 2026-10-01 web search found no published extension. Status-sensitive: re-verify after 9 Nov 2026.

original_interpretation: Effective 15 Jan 2026 BIS moved licence review for H200-class and less-advanced AI chips to China/Macau from presumption of denial to case-by-case.
evidence_found: FR 2026-00789 abstract: "changing it from a presumption of denial to a case-by-case review. The semiconductors covered by this rule are the Nvidia H200 and its equivalents, as well as less advanced chips"; "The effective date of this rule is January 15, 2026." (91 FR 1684). BIS release: "BIS will now review export license applications for the Nvidia H200, AMD MI325X, and similar chips on a case-by-case basis"
notes: Thresholds: TPP < 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth < 6,500 GB/s; chips must be commercially available in the US. Presumption of denial kept for entities headquartered in Macau/D:5 when exported elsewhere. BIS press release is dated January 14, 2026 (not 13 Jan as recorded on SRC-0114); see updates.jsonl.

original_interpretation: Case-by-case approval needs conditions incl. independent third-party testing in the US and evidence exports won't reduce capacity available to US customers.
evidence_found: BIS release (14 Jan 2026): "license applicants must demonstrate that exporting these products to China will not reduce global semiconductor production capacity currently available to U.S. customers; that the Chinese purchaser has adopted export compliance procedures, including customer screening; and that the product has undergone independent, third-party testing in the United States to verify its performance and security."
notes: Rule text adds further conditions: sufficient US supply/no delay to US orders, aggregate China/Macau shipments no more than 50% of US shipments of that product, KYC procedures, and lab review of every shipment (sampling allowed).

original_interpretation: 13 May 2025 BIS said it would not enforce and would formally rescind the Jan 2025 AI Diffusion Rule (compliance date 15 May 2025).
evidence_found: "The AI Diffusion Rule was issued on January 15, 2025, with compliance requirements that were set to come into effect on May 15, 2025."; "BIS plans to publish a regulation formalizing the rescission and will issue a replacement rule in the future."; "Kessler has instructed BIS enforcement officials not to enforce the Biden Administration's AI Diffusion Rule" (BIS press release, May 13, 2025)
notes: Federal Register API search (BIS, 'Artificial Intelligence Diffusion') on 2026-10-01 returned no standalone rescission rule; the Unified Agenda (RIN 0694-AJ90) listed formal rescission as Final Action 07/2026. Whether the 14 Jul 2026 UAE rule (FR 2026-14132) formally rescinds it was not checked. A PDF version on media.bis.gov is dated May 12, 2025.

original_interpretation: With the rescission BIS issued guidance on risks of certain Huawei Ascend chips and on diversion of US AI chips.
evidence_found: "Issuing guidance alerting industry to the risks of using PRC advanced computing ICs, including specific Huawei Ascend chips."; "Issuing guidance warning the public about the potential consequences of allowing U.S. AI chips to be used for training and inference of Chinese AI models."; "Issuing guidance to U.S. companies on how to protect supply chains against diversion tactics." (BIS press release, 13 May 2025)
notes: An earlier PDF version of the release (media.bis.gov, dated May 12) said the guidance was that 'using Huawei Ascend chips anywhere in the world violates U.S. export controls'; the live web version uses the softer 'risks' wording that this claim follows.

original_interpretation: CHIPS and Science Act 2022 gives Commerce USD 52.7bn over five years.
evidence_found: "The CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 provides the Department of Commerce with $52.7 billion over five years to develop programs and activities to boost semiconductor manufacturing and research in the United States" (NIST CHIPS for America Fact Sheet, March 18, 2024, p.1)
notes: NIST URL redirects to the PDF 'Fact Sheet - Federal Incentives-updated-508C.pdf' dated March 18, 2024; source publication_date updated in updates.jsonl.

original_interpretation: USD 39bn to CHIPS Program Office for manufacturing incentives, USD 11bn to CHIPS R&D Office.
evidence_found: "the CHIPS Program Office responsible for $39 billion in incentives to encourage investment in facilities and equipment in the United States, and the CHIPS Research and Development (R&D) Office responsible for $11 billion to develop a robust domestic R&D ecosystem" (NIST fact sheet, 18 Mar 2024, p.1)
notes: Allocation as described in March 2024; later reprogramming of CHIPS funds under the 2025 Investment Accelerator was not checked.

original_interpretation: NIST fact sheet describes the CHIPS ITC as up to 25% of qualified capex.
evidence_found: "The Department of Treasury is implementing a CHIPS Investment Tax Credit (ITC) ... The ITC is expected to be up to 25% of qualified capital expenditures." (NIST fact sheet dated March 18, 2024, p.3)
correction: The fact sheet (Mar 2024) does say this, but the rate is outdated: P.L. 119-21 s.70308 raised the 48D rate to 35% for property placed in service after 31 Dec 2025 (26 USC 48D(a): 'an amount equal to 35 percent of the qualified investment'); 25% now applies only to property placed in service before 2026 (IRS Form 3468 instructions correction). See CLM-0315.
notes: Quote accurate; marked outdated so the 25% figure is not used as the current rate.

original_interpretation: NIST guardrails rule (15 CFR 231, effective 24 Nov 2023) bars recipients for 10 years from material expansion in a foreign country of concern and restricts joint research/tech licensing with foreign entities of concern.
evidence_found: FR: 88 FR 65600, effective 2023-11-24. Expansion Clawback: "exceptions to the prohibition on semiconductor manufacturing capacity expansions that apply to existing facilities that manufacture legacy semiconductors"; Technology Clawback "prohibits the covered entity from knowingly engaging in any joint research or technology licensing effort with a foreign entity of concern that relates to a technology or product that raises national security concerns"
correction: Needs caveats: the 10-year bar applies to the Expansion Clawback, with exceptions for legacy-chip facilities. The Technology Clawback's term is set per award in the award documents (the final rule dropped the 10-year 'applicable term' definition), and it covers only knowing joint research/licensing on technologies the Secretary has flagged as raising national security concerns. See new claim superseding CLM-0313.

original_interpretation: 48D rate is 35% after P.L. 119-21 s.70308; 25% for facilities placed in service before 2026.
evidence_found: IRS: "The advanced manufacturing investment credit is equal to 35% of the qualified investment with respect to any advanced manufacturing facility of an eligible taxpayer in the tax year, unless the facility was placed in service before 2026, in which case the credit rate is 25%. See ... P.L. 119-21, section 70308". 26 USC 48D(a): "35 percent of the qualified investment"; s.70308(b): amendments "apply to property placed in service after December 31, 2025."
notes: IRS page last updated 10-Sep-2026. The statute keys the rate to when the property is placed in service; the Form 3468 page-13 text says 'facility'. The construction-start deadline of 31 Dec 2026 still applies.

original_interpretation: 31 Mar 2025 EO created the US Investment Accelerator in Commerce, responsible for the CHIPS Program Office.
evidence_found: "the Secretary of Commerce ... shall establish within the Department of Commerce an office named the United States Investment Accelerator"; "The Investment Accelerator shall be responsible for the CHIPS Program Office within the Department of Commerce" (EO 'Establishing the United States Investment Accelerator', Sec. 3(a)-(b), March 31, 2025)
notes: The EO directed Commerce to set up the office within 30 days; the EO did not create it directly.

original_interpretation: Section 232 proclamation signed 14 Jan 2026: 25% ad valorem duty, effective 15 Jan 2026, on certain advanced computing chips and derivatives.
evidence_found: "imports of Covered Products will be subject to a 25 percent ad valorem duty rate. This tariff shall be effective with respect to goods entered for consumption ... on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern standard time on January 15, 2026"; para 10: "certain advanced computing chips and certain derivative products described in the Annex"; signed "this fourteenth day of January ... two thousand twenty-six".

original_interpretation: The Jan 2026 tariff exempts imports for US data centers, repairs, R&D, startups, non-data-center consumer and civil industrial uses, and US public sector.
evidence_found: Clause (3): "The duty rate described in this clause shall not apply to imports of those Covered Products for use in United States data centers, for repairs or replacements performed in the United States, for research and development in the United States, for use by startups, for non-data center consumer applications in the United States, for use in non-data center civil industrial applications in the United States, for use in United States public sector applications, or for other uses that the Secretary determines..."
notes: There is also a catch-all for other uses the Secretary decides strengthen the US supply chain.

original_interpretation: Jan 2026 proclamation: broader tariffs plus tariff offset programme may be considered after negotiations; market review due by 1 July 2026.
evidence_found: Clause (1): "Depending on the status or resolution of such negotiations, I may consider imposing significant tariffs on imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and their derivative products, as well as an accompanying tariff offset program"; clause (9): "By July 1, 2026, the Secretary shall provide me with an update on the market for semiconductors that are used in United States data centers, so that the President may determine whether it is appropriate to modify the tariff"
correction: Precision: the 1 July 2026 item is an update on the market for semiconductors used in US data centers, which feeds a decision on changing this tariff. Separately, an update on negotiations was due within 90 days.
notes: TechTimes (3 Sep 2026) reports the Commerce report was finished but not made public; tier 3, not relied on.

original_interpretation: As of 3 Sep 2026 the Commerce Secretary had signalled a second phase of s.232 chip tariffs but no new proclamation, rates or effective date had been published.
evidence_found: TechTimes 3 Sep 2026: "He did not announce specific tariff rates, product lists, or a phase-in timeline."; "Phase Two has not yet been finalized."; "Specific tariff rates for Phase Two have not been finalized. Product scope has not been published." Lutnick quote: companies that do not build in the US should "expect to pay to enter the greatest market in the world."
correction: The quote 'No new proclamation has been signed.' could not be found in the article. The article uses 'has not yet been finalized' wording. 'build in the United States, pay nothing; build nowhere, pay to enter the market' is the journalist's paraphrase, not a direct Lutnick quote. The status itself is supported.
notes: Tier-3 news only. claim_type 'reported_claim' is a poor fit: this is a status statement (a fact resting on news), not an entity describing itself. Newer check: the whitehouse.gov proclamations list (page 1, items 8-25 Sep 2026, viewed 2026-10-01) showed no semiconductor tariff proclamation; earlier September items and the Federal Register were not fully checked.

original_interpretation: USTR found under s.301 that China's semiconductor targeting is actionable; tariffs at 0% from 23 Dec 2025 rising 23 Jun 2027 to a rate TBA.
evidence_found: "China's targeting of the semiconductor industry for dominance is unreasonable and burdens or restricts U.S. commerce and thus is actionable."; "taking tariff action now on semiconductors from China, with an initial tariff level of 0 percent, increasing in 18 months on June 23, 2027, to a rate to be announced not fewer than 30 days prior to that date"; "December 23, 2025: The effective date of the action." (90 FR 60848)

original_interpretation: s.301 investigation initiated 23 Dec 2024; action covers 18 tariff lines incl. wafers, transistors, diodes, thyristors, ICs, on top of existing 50% s.301 tariff.
evidence_found: "On December 23, 2024, the U.S. Trade Representative initiated a section 301 investigation"; "These new Section 301 tariffs would be additional to the existing 50 percent Section 301 tariff on semiconductors from China"; "This action applies to the following 8-digit subheadings" - table lists 18 codes (2804.61.00 ... 8542.90.00).
notes: Counted 18 subheadings myself. They also include high-purity silicon (2804.61), doped wafers/discs (3818.00), photosensitive devices and parts of ICs.

original_interpretation: Treasury OISP, effective 2 Jan 2025, prohibits or requires notification of certain US-person investments in Chinese (incl. HK, Macau) entities in semis, quantum and AI.
evidence_found: "directs the Secretary of the Treasury ... to establish a program to prohibit or require notification of certain types of outbound investments by United States persons"; "semiconductors and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, and artificial intelligence"; "China, along with ... Hong Kong and Macau"; final rule "with an effective date of January 2, 2025." (Treasury OISP page)
notes: Newer context, from secondary sources only (not opened as primary): the COINS Act (FY2026 NDAA, signed 18 Dec 2025) put the program into statute and expands it. Treasury implementing rules are due by Mar 2027, and the current rules stay in force until then. Worth a follow-up claim from the statute.

original_interpretation: EU Chips Act, Reg (EU) 2023/1781 of 13 Sep 2023, entered into force 21 Sep 2023.
evidence_found: EUR-Lex: "REGULATION (EU) 2023/1781 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 September 2023 ... (Chips Act)", "OJ L 229, 18.9.2023", "In force"; Commission page: "It entered into force on 21 September 2023."

original_interpretation: EU Chips Act has three pillars: Chips for Europe Initiative; security of supply and resilience; monitoring and crisis response.
evidence_found: "### Pillar I - The \"Chips for Europe\" Initiative"; "### Pillar II - Security of supply and resilience"; "### Pillar III - Monitoring and crisis response" (Commission European Chips Act page, 'three pillars of action')

original_interpretation: Commission approved 18 State aid decisions for first-of-a-kind chip facilities, >EUR 32bn public+private investment (page accessed 2026-09-29).
evidence_found: "The Commission has already approved **18** **State aid decisions** on first-of-a-kind semiconductor facilities that represent a total **public and private investment** of over EUR 32 billion" (Commission Chips Act page, Pillar II, re-read 2026-10-01)
notes: Unchanged on 2026-10-01. In the page's table only 8 of the 18 rows give amounts, and these add up to about EUR 32.2bn (ESMC listed as '>10'). The rest show '-', so the total is a lower bound.

original_interpretation: Commission proposed Chips Act 2.0 on 3 June 2026; a proposal, not adopted law as of sources read.
evidence_found: Library page: "Publication 03 June 2026 ... The Commission has adopted a proposal for the Chips Act 2.0, which introduces new measures to further boost the chips industry, reduce strategic dependencies and support advanced chip production in the EU." Chips Act page: "the Chips Act 2.0, proposed by the Commission in June 2026"
notes: Where it stands in Parliament/Council not checked; both Commission pages still call it a proposal as of 2026-10-01.

original_interpretation: SEMI said Chips Act 2.0 priorities include expanding first-of-a-kind, accelerating R&D uptake, streamlining permitting, stimulating demand.
evidence_found: "We welcome the Chips Act 2.0's ambition to expand the 'first-of-a-kind' concept, accelerate the industrial uptake of R&D, streamline permitting procedures, and stimulate demand across the semiconductor value chain," said Laith Altimime, President of SEMI Europe. (SEMI press release, Brussels, June 3, 2026)
notes: This is SEMI Europe's description of the proposal. reported_claim is the right type.
